transcript:
[00:00] Miles (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we have about 60 minutes. Quick intro round.
[00:08] Liam (CedarBank): Hey Liam here, Head of AI at CedarBank. Priya, Jason and Evelyn from our team.
[00:15] Miles: Great. Samira, you wanna kick into the technical asks?
[00:18] Samira (Redwood SE): Sure, thanks. So the goal for today's call is to scope the POC: define success criteria, figure workload sizing and benchmarks, and then decide which deployment mode makes sense — hosted API, dedicated reserved capacity, or private (VPC/on-prem). We'll walk through traffic patterns, latency needs, security constraints.
[00:35] Evelyn (CedarBank PM): For context, we want to launch a conversational assistant for payments workflows — balance inquiries, dispute triage, and some autocompletion for agent notes. The business wants <200ms generation latency for short prompts, and high throughput during morning peak.
[00:50] Jason (Platform): Current infra is GCP with a mix of on-prem legacy for sensitive data. We have strict egress rules. Any external calls have to go through our approved gateways.
[00:59] Priya (SecOps): We're SOC2 in progress, and need to ensure keys and PII handling is auditable. KMS integration and customer-controlled keys are big ask.
[01:07] Samira: Good — those are classic decision drivers. Quick Qs on volume: Liam, what's your daily conversational volume and token distribution?
[01:14] Liam: Expected initial volume ~ 10k sessions/day, median prompt length 30 tokens, average completion 60 tokens, but some long-form backfills for transcripts ~1k tokens. Peak concurrency estimated 150-250 concurrent requests.
[01:29] Samira: Ok that's helpful. For 150-250 concurrent at that token size, you can either go Hosted if you want fastest time-to-value and are OK with standard multi-tenant SLAs; Dedicated if you want reserved GPU pools for predictable latency; or Private if you need full network isolation / on-prem.
[01:44] Miles: I'll add cost framing — Hosted is pay-as-you-go with lower upfront but variable unit costs. Dedicated is a commit monthly with lower per-token cost and predictable throughput. Private has the highest ops and project cost but meets strict compliance and network constraints.
[01:58] Jason: Our main blocker is egress and the on-prem data for disputes. We could anonymize/sample data for initial eval but production needs some workloads in our VPC.
[02:07] Priya: Also KMS. We need BYOK with HSM-backed keys or at least customer-managed KMS integration.
[02:14] Samira: We support KMS integrations in Dedicated and Private modes; Hosted supports envelope encryption and Redwood-managed keys but we can discuss bringing your key via customer-managed KMS (there are additional steps). We'll include exact requirements in the security pack.
[02:28] Evelyn: Success criteria from product: 95% of responses must be within acceptance thresholds — latency <200ms for short turns, accuracy measured with our prompt set F1 > 0.85 for entity extraction, and cost per ticket below $0.75.
[02:41] Miles: That's helpful — can you share the prompt set and a few labeled examples? We can bake that into the benchmark.
[02:47] Liam: We'll share a PII-sanitized set by next Monday.
[02:50] Samira: For benchmarking, recommended approach: 1) dry-run on Hosted to validate model/ops quickly, 2) run dedicated benchmark with same model architecture on 4-GPU Dedicated to measure latency at concurrency, 3) if VPC/on-prem constraints remain, run a Private deploy trial in your lab or our private instance. We'll provide a benchmark template with synthetic traffic and a CSV for results.
[03:12] Jason: What's realistic performance on 4xA100 for your recommended model?
[03:16] Samira: Rough numbers — for a 7B-ish LLM under quantized execution: tail latency 95th percentile ~80-150ms for 60-token completions with batching tuned; throughput for continuous inference variable but should support your 150-250 conc with a small autoscale headroom. For 1k-token backfills you'll want separate batch jobs or different instance sizing. These are estimates, we'll run a proper perf test.
[03:36] Liam: Cost ballpark for Dedicated vs Hosted?
[03:39] Miles: Hosted: higher per-token but zero infra ops. Dedicated: commit to reservation, lower per-token, predictable. Private: setup and ongoing ops — higher capex and integration time. We'll send a pricing matrix.
[03:50] Priya: Data residency — we need logs to remain in EU region for EU customers. Can Redwood pin Hosted to EU?
[03:57] Samira: Yes Hosted can be regionally pinned for data at rest, but Dedicated and Private give stronger guarantees and tooling for audit logs. We'll document retention controls.
[04:06] Evelyn: Timeline — product wants POC in 6 weeks, decision on production mode in 8-10 weeks. Is that feasible?
[04:12] Samira: Typical POC timeline: Week 0-1: requirements + data exchange; Week 2: initial Hosted proof-of-concept and quick smoke tests; Week 3-4: Dedicated perf benchmark and tuning; Week 5-6: security review and, if needed, Private deploy trial. So 6 weeks for an initial POC is tight but doable if data and benchmark assets are provided quickly.
[04:31] Miles: We'll prioritize hosted proof-of-value to accelerate. If you need private bits we can spin up a limited Private review in parallel.
[04:37] Jason: For benchmarking we'll need the exact API contract and a runner tool. Do you have a benchmarking repo?
[04:42] Samira: Yes, we'll share our benchmark harness and a sample load script (k6/gatling style) and a template for results to compare latency/throughput.
[04:50] Liam: What are failure modes? We care about fallback if Dedicated capacity spikes out.
[04:54] Samira: Redwood supports smart routing and fallback policies — you can route to a cheaper Hosted or different model if Dedicated capacity is congested. We'll show policy examples and circuit-breakers in the playbook.
[05:04] Priya: Audit logs — we need immutable logs for requests containing user identifiers. Is that in Dedicated/Private?
[05:10] Samira: Audit logs and per-token tracing available in Dedicated and Private, and we can extend retention for enterprise add-ons. For Hosted we have logs but with standard retention windows; enterprise retention is an add-on.
[05:20] Miles: Quick recap of decision criteria we typically see: 1) If you need fastest launch and are ok with platform-managed keys, Hosted. 2) If you need predictable throughput/cost and lower per-token, Dedicated. 3) If you have strict network/compliance or must keep keys/certs on-prem, Private. Also hybrid: start Hosted, migrate heavy/PII traffic to Dedicated or Private.
[05:40] Evelyn: That hybrid path sounds appealing — could we start Hosted for agent-facing features and keep dispute processing in Private?
[05:45] Samira: Absolutely — routing by route or model variant is supported. We can implement prefix caching for repeated queries to keep cost low.
[05:52] Jason: For the POC we want concrete numbers: run a perf test at 150, 250, 500 concurrent with 30/60 token mixes and report 50/95/99 latencies, and cost per 1,000 tokens.
[06:05] Samira: Noted. We'll run those and include both Dedicated and Hosted runs where possible.
[06:10] Miles: Ok next steps, we'll send security docs and pricing, Samira you'll run the perf estimate and share benchmark harness. CedarBank to share sanitized dataset + prompts. Book follow-up for 7/27 for network review.
[06:23] Liam: Sounds good. Thanks all.
[06:26] Miles: Thanks, we'll send notes and action items.
[06:30] [END]

Notes: transcript contains minor transcription artifacts (names sometimes mis-heard), occasional run-on sentences. References: shared deck (link: /redwood/deck/cedarbank-poc.pdf), benchmark repo (link: https://github.com/redwood/benchmarks/cedarbank-sample).
